heading: Tuesday, October 6, 2026
topLine: 3 stories on AI and open problems: OpenAI's 722 manuscripts, Quasi-Riemann hypothesis and Erdős site freezes claims. Also: 2 model releases: Google Nano Banana 2.1 and Mistral AI Mistral Large 4.

items.headline: OpenAI releases 722 AI-written manuscripts claiming 377 results on open questions
items.summary: OpenAI posted 722 papers on GitHub, grouped into about 372–377 result families, from an unreleased internal model that attempted about 4,000 problems. Each result used an average of about three hours of Pro-level compute. The 722 are manuscripts, not 722 solved problems. OpenAI says about 42% of the top-line results have Lean formalizations, and the rest are unverified. Within days, three algebraic geometry papers were withdrawn over a sign error, and Johan Commelin said some formalizations prove weaker statements than the papers claim. Mathematicians including Daniel Litt suggested treating the papers as raw research findings for now.

items.headline: OpenAI model proves a zero-free strip for the Riemann zeta function
items.summary: Among OpenAI's 6 October release was a proof of a "quasi-Riemann hypothesis": all nontrivial zeta zeros have real part between 1/8 and 7/8 (Lean-verified). A later version, edited by a human, narrows the strip to between 1/12 and 11/12 but has not been formally verified. Experts quoted by Quanta largely agree the result is correct. Peter Sarnak won't call it a theorem until humans check all the details, and Maksym Radziwiłł found the papers poorly written. Jared Duker Lichtman called it the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far.

items.headline: erdosproblems.com freezes proof claims and drops solved/open labels
items.summary: Thomas Bloom suspended new problem comments and proof claims on erdosproblems.com. He said unexplained AI-generated proofs had become the main public activity and displaced human discussion. The site will also hide open/solved statuses, stop using credit language for any solver, human or AI, and prioritise human expositions. Bloom described the hiatus as experimental, and Terence Tao cross-posted the announcement.

items.headline: Google releases Nano Banana 2.1 image model
items.summary: Nano Banana 2.1 updates Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image). Google says it improves visual quality, prompt adherence, multi-turn character consistency and text rendering while keeping Flash-level speed and cost. It is generally available in the Gemini API as gemini-nano-banana-2.1.

items.headline: Mistral previews Mistral Large 4, a 1T-parameter open-weight model
items.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a natively multimodal hybrid instruct-and-reasoning mixture-of-experts model with about 1 trillion total and 52B active parameters, trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. It launched as a public preview on Mistral's API at $1.36/$4.18 per million input/output tokens, with open weights promised for later in October.
